outcome: patient experiences after obstetric anal sphincter injury (themes: pain control, desire for multifactorial support, OASI knowledge and awareness)
postnatal depression (screened positive on Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale)
cohort: Fifteen women with a mean age of 31 years who experienced an obstetric anal sphincter injury within a tertiary care network participated.
finding: The study identified three major themes regarding patient experiences after obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI): pain control, desire for multifactorial support, and OASI knowledge and awareness, highlighting opportunities for improved postpartum care.
cross-section timing: Data was collected between May and June of 2022
